step1_analysis.description: A 5-transistor PMOS-input operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with an NMOS current mirror load. Note: The output node was erroneously extracted as 'GND' in the provided netlist (drains of XM2 and XM4) and has been corrected to 'OUT' in the testbench to allow proper operation and measurement.

paper_reference.title: Design of a Low-Noise Preamplifier for Nerve Cuff Electrode Recording

power_consumption.description: Total power consumed by the circuit

sky130_expected.reasoning: A 500uA tail current is chosen to approximate the paper's power consumption within the 1.8V SKY130 supply limit.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm1 = 500uS, Rout = ro_p || ro_n = 40kOhm. Gain = gm1 * Rout = 20 V/V = 26 dB
sky130_expected.reasoning: Open-loop gain of a single-stage OTA in 130nm is typically 20-30 dB due to the low intrinsic gain (gm*ro) of short-channel devices.
Open-loop UGBW is much higher than the closed-loop bandwidth reported in the paper, determined primarily by gm and load capacitance.

sky130_expected.calculation: Single pole system with 1pF load, non-dominant poles are at high frequencies.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A single-stage OTA with a 1pF load typically has a phase margin close to 90 degrees.

input_noise_1kHz.description: Input-referred noise spectral density at 1 kHz

sky130_expected.calculation: Thermal noise = sqrt(1.65e-20 * (4/3) * (1/500e-6) * (1 + 2.32)) = 12 nV/sqrt(Hz). Flicker noise will increase this at 1kHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS has lower gm and higher flicker noise than the BJT input pair used in the paper's BiCMOS process, resulting in higher expected noise.

total_input_noise.description: Total integrated input-referred noise from 1 Hz to 10 kHz

sky130_expected.calculation: Integration of ~25 nV/sqrt(Hz) over 10kHz bandwidth = 25e-9 * sqrt(10000) = 2.5 uV rms.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Higher noise spectral density in CMOS compared to BiCMOS leads to higher integrated noise.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench for measuring open-loop gain, UGBW, phase margin, power, noise, and transient response of the OTA using a large L-C feedback network to maintain DC bias while allowing open-loop AC characterization.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Design of a Low-Noise Preamplifier for Nerve Cuff Electrode Recording
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u

* DUT (Note: GND on XM2 and XM4 drains corrected to OUT)
XM3 N0 N0 VSS GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM2 OUT VIN_MINUS N1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM4 OUT N0 VSS GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM1 N0 VIN_PLUS N1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

* Tail current source
Itail VDD N1 500u

* Load capacitor
CL OUT 0 1p

* Supplies and Bias
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSS VSS 0 0
VCM VIN_PLUS 0 0.9

* DC feedback for open-loop AC analysis
* Lfb shorts OUT to VIN_MINUS at DC, opens at AC
* Cac couples AC input to VIN_MINUS, opens at DC
Lfb OUT VIN_MINUS 1MEG
Cac VIN_AC VIN_MINUS 1
Vac VIN_AC 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 SIN(0.9 1m 100k 0 0)

.control
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

ac dec 100 1 100MEG
let gain_db = vdb(OUT)
let phase_deg = 180/PI * cph(v(OUT))
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=1
meas ac ugbw when gain_db=0 fall=1
meas ac phase_at_ugbw find phase_deg when gain_db=0 fall=1

noise v(OUT) Vac dec 100 1 10k
setplot noise1
meas noise inoise_1k find inoise_spectrum at=1k
setplot noise2
let inoise_rms = sqrt(inoise_total)
print inoise_rms

tran 0.1u 20u
meas tran v_max max v(OUT)
meas tran v_min min v(OUT)
let v_pp = v_max - v_min
print v_pp

quit
.endc
.end
